opening_message:
Ticket 1: Traci Lowe (employee ID E041) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E041.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Traci Lowe (E041) is a full-time Analyst. Requested admin on Source Code, but admin is only for the owning role (Engineer). As a full-time employee, max is write. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Traci Lowe (E041) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors max is read (write requires advanced training; never admin). Requested admin on Source Code, so grant max read.
reason: Traci Lowe (E041) requested admin on Source Code. The notes conflict on employment status: HR lists full-time, but Security lists contractor with basic security training (both stating they looked this up). Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, and Traci is an Analyst, so admin is not permitted in either interpretation. Under the Security-verified contractor status with basic training, the maximum is read (write requires advanced training; contractors never get admin). I grant the more restrictive verified maximum: read.
